rulings.raw: 3 to 3 ½ pounds Boneless Eye of Round Roast
rulings.evidence: Whole-muscle beef round roast; board carries no commodity and no capture, so a new id is proposed. 1474 g (range midpoint) yields 43 g protein per serving against the source's published 40 g.

rulings.raw: Kosher Salt & Freshly Cracked Black Pepper (- to taste)
rulings.term: Kosher Salt & Freshly Cracked Black Pepper
rulings.evidence: One line carrying two pantry seasonings; costed as salt (priced 7/7) with the black pepper noted as pantry-static rather than split into a phantom line.
Unsalted is the same product concept, same 4-stick pack and same price class as the `butter` id, and the gram weight per tablespoon is identical - not a form flip.

rulings.raw: 1 tsp Finely Chopped Fresh Rosemary ((substitute: ½ tsp Dried))
rulings.evidence: fresh-rosemary is already a live board id (5/7 stores), so this is a reuse needing only a vocabulary row; dried rosemary is a different price and a different gram weight per teaspoon.

rulings.raw: 2 tsp Chopped Fresh Thyme ((substitute: 1 tsp Dried))
rulings.evidence: fresh-thyme is a live board id (4/7); refusing the bridge to dried-thyme because 2 tsp fresh is 1.6 g of herb against about 2 g of dried leaf at a different price.
Same food as the chopped line; a thyme sprig weighs about 1 g.
A rosemary sprig weighs about 2 g; same live board id as the chopped line.

Baby bella is its own 8 oz tray at a premium over the white-button `mushrooms` id (whose vocabulary label is White Mushrooms), and portobello is the mature large cap sold by the 2-count - variety pricing, same class of call as red onion vs onions.
red-wine is a live board id (4/7 stores) - a reuse, not a proposal; the vocabulary only lacks the name row. Red wine vinegar is a different food and is refused.

rulings.raw: 2 ½ Cups No Sodium Beef Stock ((substitute: no-sodium beef broth))
rulings.evidence: The source itself offers no-sodium beef broth as the substitute; beef-broth is the same carton class and is priced 7/7. Sodium level is not a price class.

new_commodity_proposals.evidence: Board reports ABSENT: no commodity and no capture match. Not already priced under another spelling - the meat ids in play are ground-beef-8020 and cube/steak cuts; an eye of round is a whole-muscle roasting joint sold by the piece at roast prices, not a ground or steak SKU. No word-order variant (round roast / eye round) appears on the everyday board or the feed.

Priced separately from `mushrooms` (vocabulary label: White Mushrooms) and from `portobello-mushrooms` (large caps sold 2-count). Baby bella/cremini is its own 8 oz tray SKU at a premium to white button - the same variety-pricing call the estate already makes for red onion vs onions. If the registrar judges the premium immaterial, aliasing to `mushrooms` is the acceptable fallback.
